caption:
A single sensor type does not carry the mission. Synthetic-aperture radar runs wide-area passes on a fixed revisit schedule, covering the full area of interest regardless of weather. When a pass flags something worth a closer look, that site can be cued for a tighter, more frequent watch.

The limit: cueing is a decision, not a switch. Re-tasking a narrower watch onto a specific site takes time to plan and execute — it does not happen inside the same pass that generated the flag. Between the flag and the follow-up look, the site is uncovered.

That gap is real and it is priced into how findings are labeled. A flag from a wide pass is a lead. Confirmation waits for the next dedicated look — and the interval between them is stated, not hidden.
thread: Wide-area radar passes run on schedule. When one flags a site, that site can be cued for a tighter follow-up watch. That's the capability.
The limit: cueing takes a decision cycle to execute. It is not an instant re-task. Between the flag and the follow-up pass, the site sits uncovered.
A flag from a wide pass is a lead, not confirmation. The interval to the next dedicated look is stated as part of the finding, not smoothed over.
Coverage gaps between cueing and follow-up are the honest cost of a wide-area collection plan. Naming them is what keeps the next flag credible.

card.headline: A flag earns a closer look, not an instant one
card.sub: Re-tasking a tighter watch onto a cued site takes a decision cycle. The gap between flag and follow-up is stated, not hidden.

rationale: Introduces the tasking/cueing distinction (unused angle) with an explicit, undramatized limit about re-tasking latency, avoiding overlap with prior revisit/quiet-cycle posts.
